assets.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: Godot game player ship sprite. Reference image: use ONLY as style and boat construction reference. Create one isolated ancient Greek rowing ship viewed from directly overhead, orthographic top-down camera with a small readable deck perspective. Long axis horizontal, stern on LEFT, pointed bronze ram/prow on RIGHT. Dark warm brown wooden hull, wooden deck, symmetric oars extending to both sides, one mast with cream square sail edged in crimson Greek meander like reference, bronze fittings, small crimson stern banner. Rich crisp hand-clustered PIXEL ART, dark outlines, readable 16-bit game sprite, restrained dithering, actual stepped pixels, no photorealism. Ship occupies 85 percent of horizontal canvas, centered, all oars inside canvas with margin. Hull itself is slender, oars add width. Transparent alpha background: no ocean, no waves, no shadow plane, no text, no border, no additional ships. This sprite must be suitable for rotation and scaling to around 160px wide in a storm navigation game.

Use case: stylized-concept. Godot top-down pixel-art island game sprite for Greek Odyssey storm navigation. Single isolated rugged Mediterranean rocky island viewed orthographically from overhead, no horizon. Broad crescent shape with open sheltered cove entering from LEFT, inviting sand beach inside cove, green cypresses and olive trees on upper/right slopes, layered dark slate cliffs, pale sand, moss, small ancient Greek stone stairway. Match reference rich dark pixel-art clusters and dithered rocky textures. Stepped crisp pixels rather than realistic painting. Entire island fits frame with transparent margins; real alpha transparency OUTSIDE island and inside sea cove, no rectangular sea/background, no text, no people, no buildings, no UI. Readable small game terrain sprite about 800 pixels wide at runtime. Top-down view, cove opens LEFT toward approaching ship.

Use case: stylized-concept. Godot game hazard sprite, one vertical strip of a breaking storm wave viewed orthographically from directly ABOVE. Reference is style/palette reference only. Crisp richly detailed 16-bit PIXEL ART consistent with the reference ocean: white and ice-blue turbulent foam along the LEFT edge, thick turquoise curling crest behind it, deep navy churning water fading to real alpha transparency along the RIGHT. Wave travels LEFT, long crest runs vertically from top to bottom. Use a tall rectangular composition, a continuous wavy front spanning the ENTIRE height with no caps at top/bottom so it can repeat vertically. Foam detail and dithered pixel clusters, crisp stepped edges, no smooth gradients, no horizon, no perspective vista, no ship, no land, no words/UI. Transparent alpha around LEFT and RIGHT of the strip. Only one wave strip, not a scene. Keep white foam crest around horizontal 20 percent of width so runtime physical front can line up with it. Top and bottom edges should match for seamless vertical repetition.

Use case: stylized-concept. Godot top-down Greek Odyssey game obstacle sprite. Reference image is style and palette reference only. One isolated cluster of rugged dark slate Mediterranean rocks, small reef emerging above the water, viewed orthographically from above with slight readable rock-face perspective matching reference. Irregular roughly round footprint, a larger central boulder and 3 smaller attached outcrops. Rich detailed crisp PIXEL ART with stepped stone shapes and gray-blue angular facets, weathered cracks, sparse olive moss, wet highlights, restrained dithering. Natural silhouette, not a geometric regular polygon. Small wisps of white sea foam around the bottom edge only. True transparent alpha outside the rocks, no sea rectangular background, no landmass, no trees, no UI/text, no people. One centered sprite with clear transparent margin all around, occupies 80 percent of square canvas. Suitable for scaling to 110px wide while preserving readable pixel clusters.
